records.name: Active recall from a blank page
records.definition: Reconstruct a topic outline without notes, then verify and correct omissions.

target_performance.statement: Reconstruct the structure and important relationships of a recently studied topic without looking at notes, then compare against a trusted source and repair omissions.
target_performance.metric: Given a one-page topic previously studied, produce a map containing the central idea, at least five key elements and at least three correct relationships. Score each element for accuracy and each relationship for direction/meaning. Pass the initial check when all central ideas are accurate and at least 80% of essential elements and relationships are correct; verify again on a different day.
target_performance.conditions: Choose a bounded topic that has already been studied; do not use a topic never understood. Prepare blank paper and the source material for later checking. Before recall, write the topic and a confidence prediction (low/medium/high).

success_criteria.statement: Reconstruct the structure and important relationships of a recently studied topic without looking at notes, then compare against a trusted source and repair omissions.
success_criteria.threshold_text: Given a one-page topic previously studied, produce a map containing the central idea, at least five key elements and at least three correct relationships. Score each element for accuracy and each relationship for direction/meaning. Pass the initial check when all central ideas are accurate and at least 80% of essential elements and relationships are correct; verify again on a different day.

steps: Close all notes and write the central question or topic title.
Spend 3–5 minutes drawing or listing everything remembered, grouping related ideas rather than copying remembered sentences.
Add arrows or short phrases showing causal, hierarchical or sequential relationships.
Mark uncertain items with a question mark instead of guessing confidently.
Open the source and compare line by line: mark accurate recall, missing essentials, distorted relationships and unsupported additions in four different ways.
Close the source and reconstruct only the missed or distorted parts.
Finish by writing two questions that would expose the most important remaining gap.
practice_protocol.frequency_per_week: Use one 10–15 minute cycle per topic. One cycle is enough for an initial attempt; repeat only the weak sections after feedback. Do not turn the task into a speed contest.
practice_protocol.environment: Choose a bounded topic that has already been studied; do not use a topic never understood

assessment.method: Given a one-page topic previously studied, produce a map containing the central idea, at least five key elements and at least three correct relationships. Score each element for accuracy and each relationship for direction/meaning. Pass the initial check when all central ideas are accurate and at least 80% of essential elements and relationships are correct; verify again on a different day.
assessment.record: A dated recall map, source used, marked error categories, unaided delayed map, and brief transfer explanation.

maintenance.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance.protocol: After 24–72 hours, perform a cold reconstruction without review immediately beforehand. If the central structure is missing or accuracy falls below the agreed threshold, mark needs_revision and target only the failed links.

maintenance_policy.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance_policy.protocol: After 24–72 hours, perform a cold reconstruction without review immediately beforehand. If the central structure is missing or accuracy falls below the agreed threshold, mark needs_revision and target only the failed links.
maintenance_policy.scheduler_note: A review interval is earned by performance evidence, not assigned from category alone.

safety_notes: Cognitive; no physical safety concern. Protect privacy if the topic contains personal or confidential information. Use a reliable source for the correction stage.

records.name: Confidence calibration
records.definition: Predict confidence before checking an answer and compare it with correctness.

target_performance.statement: Estimate the probability that an answer is correct before feedback, then compare confidence with observed accuracy over repeated, varied questions.
target_performance.metric: Across at least 30 varied items over multiple sessions, confidence should become meaningfully ordered: higher-confidence groups should generally have higher accuracy. Pass is not “100% accuracy”; it is honest estimates, fewer unjustified 95–100% claims and an ability to explain sources of miscalibration.
target_performance.conditions: Use practice questions with answer keys or an independent checker. Separate confidence in the answer from confidence in the explanation. Avoid using emotionally loaded or high-stakes decisions for early practice.

success_criteria.statement: Estimate the probability that an answer is correct before feedback, then compare confidence with observed accuracy over repeated, varied questions.
success_criteria.threshold_text: Across at least 30 varied items over multiple sessions, confidence should become meaningfully ordered: higher-confidence groups should generally have higher accuracy. Pass is not “100% accuracy”; it is honest estimates, fewer unjustified 95–100% claims and an ability to explain sources of miscalibration.

steps: Answer a small set of 10 questions without checking.
Before revealing feedback, assign each answer a probability such as 50%, 70%, 90% or 100%; do not use “sure” without a number.
Record a one-line reason for high-confidence answers.
Check answers against the key and classify each as correct/incorrect.
Group answers by confidence band (for example 60–69%, 70–79%, 80–89%, 90–100%) and compare stated confidence with actual accuracy.
Inspect high-confidence errors first: identify missing knowledge, misread wording, faulty reasoning or unjustified assumption.
Repeat with a fresh set and adjust confidence estimates only when evidence supports the adjustment.
practice_protocol.frequency_per_week: Use 10–20 questions per session, two or three sessions per topic. Avoid overinterpreting small samples; confidence calibration improves through repeated observations, not one quiz.
practice_protocol.environment: Use practice questions with answer keys or an independent checker

assessment.method: Across at least 30 varied items over multiple sessions, confidence should become meaningfully ordered: higher-confidence groups should generally have higher accuracy. Pass is not “100% accuracy”; it is honest estimates, fewer unjustified 95–100% claims and an ability to explain sources of miscalibration.
assessment.record: Question set and answer key, pre-feedback confidence per item, correctness, confidence-band summary, error explanations and delayed comparison.

maintenance.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance.protocol: Repeat a short unseen set after one week. Compare calibration patterns, not just raw score. Keep earlier data to show whether overconfidence is changing.

maintenance_policy.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance_policy.protocol: Repeat a short unseen set after one week. Compare calibration patterns, not just raw score. Keep earlier data to show whether overconfidence is changing.
maintenance_policy.scheduler_note: A review interval is earned by performance evidence, not assigned from category alone.

safety_notes: Do not use this as a diagnostic tool for mental health or as a substitute for professional risk assessment.

records.name: Explain a concept simply
records.definition: Explain a concept accurately in plain language without losing its key mechanism.

target_performance.statement: Give a concise explanation that preserves the mechanism, distinguishes examples from the rule, and survives a novice’s follow-up questions.
target_performance.metric: A novice can paraphrase the central mechanism, the explanation contains no material factual error, the example genuinely fits, and the learner correctly answers two follow-up questions. A simple explanation that omits a crucial condition does not pass.
target_performance.conditions: Select a concept the learner can already solve or use. Write its formal definition or governing model first so simplification does not become distortion.

success_criteria.statement: Give a concise explanation that preserves the mechanism, distinguishes examples from the rule, and survives a novice’s follow-up questions.
success_criteria.threshold_text: A novice can paraphrase the central mechanism, the explanation contains no material factual error, the example genuinely fits, and the learner correctly answers two follow-up questions. A simple explanation that omits a crucial condition does not pass.

steps: State the concept in one accurate sentence.
Identify the mechanism: what changes, what causes it, or what rule governs it.
Choose one familiar example that demonstrates the mechanism.
Explain the example in plain language without replacing technical terms that are essential.
State one boundary or case where the explanation would not apply.
Deliver a 60–90 second explanation without reading.
Ask a listener to paraphrase the explanation and pose two “why/how” questions.
Correct any misunderstanding, then deliver a cleaner second version.
practice_protocol.frequency_per_week: Practise one concept at a time. Make two short recordings or live explanations with feedback between them; stop when voice fatigue or frustration affects clarity.
practice_protocol.environment: Select a concept the learner can already solve or use

assessment.method: A novice can paraphrase the central mechanism, the explanation contains no material factual error, the example genuinely fits, and the learner correctly answers two follow-up questions. A simple explanation that omits a crucial condition does not pass.
assessment.record: Audio or observer notes, listener paraphrase, follow-up responses, factual correction log and delayed explanation.

maintenance.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance.protocol: Explain the concept again after several days without using the previous script. Check whether the mechanism and boundary condition remain accurate.

maintenance_policy.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance_policy.protocol: Explain the concept again after several days without using the previous script. Check whether the mechanism and boundary condition remain accurate.
maintenance_policy.scheduler_note: A review interval is earned by performance evidence, not assigned from category alone.

safety_notes: Use accurate, age-appropriate material. Do not present uncertain or disputed claims as settled facts; disclose uncertainty.

records.name: Build a useful analogy
records.definition: Map a difficult concept to a familiar system and state where the analogy breaks.

target_performance.statement: Construct an analogy that maps at least three structural relationships between a target concept and a familiar source, then identify where the mapping breaks.
target_performance.metric: Pass when at least three correspondences preserve relevant relationships, the analogy explains something that was initially difficult, at least two limits are explicit, and the learner can restate the real mechanism without relying on the analogy.
target_performance.conditions: Understand the target concept sufficiently to list its components, relationships and limits. Choose a familiar source system with comparable structure, not merely a similar appearance.

success_criteria.statement: Construct an analogy that maps at least three structural relationships between a target concept and a familiar source, then identify where the mapping breaks.
success_criteria.threshold_text: Pass when at least three correspondences preserve relevant relationships, the analogy explains something that was initially difficult, at least two limits are explicit, and the learner can restate the real mechanism without relying on the analogy.

steps: Write the target concept’s key elements and how they interact.
Select a familiar source system.
Create a two-column mapping of target element to source element.
For each mapping, state the shared relationship (for example flow, constraint, feedback or hierarchy).
Test the analogy against an ordinary case and an edge case.
Write at least two explicit limits: what the source system does that the target does not, or vice versa.
Revise any mapping that causes a false inference.
Present the analogy and then restate the target concept without the analogy.
practice_protocol.frequency_per_week: Build one analogy per concept in 10–20 minutes. Prefer one accurate analogy over several decorative ones.
practice_protocol.environment: Understand the target concept sufficiently to list its components, relationships and limits

assessment.method: Pass when at least three correspondences preserve relevant relationships, the analogy explains something that was initially difficult, at least two limits are explicit, and the learner can restate the real mechanism without relying on the analogy.
assessment.record: Target model, analogy mapping table, two limits, edge-case test, listener feedback and delayed restatement.

maintenance.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance.protocol: After a delay, explain the target concept without seeing the analogy, then reconstruct the analogy and its limits.

maintenance_policy.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance_policy.protocol: After a delay, explain the target concept without seeing the analogy, then reconstruct the analogy and its limits.
maintenance_policy.scheduler_note: A review interval is earned by performance evidence, not assigned from category alone.

safety_notes: No special safety concern; check that examples do not embed stereotypes or misleading claims.

records.name: Spot a hidden assumption
records.definition: Identify an unstated premise supporting a claim.

target_performance.statement: Identify an unstated premise that must be true for a claim or argument to work, and test whether the premise is supported.
target_performance.metric: Given five arguments, identify a relevant necessary or highly material assumption in at least four, explain why it matters, and distinguish it from a merely possible assumption.
target_performance.conditions: Use short, non-sensitive claims with enough context to interpret. Distinguish an assumption from a fact explicitly stated in the argument.

success_criteria.statement: Identify an unstated premise that must be true for a claim or argument to work, and test whether the premise is supported.
success_criteria.threshold_text: Given five arguments, identify a relevant necessary or highly material assumption in at least four, explain why it matters, and distinguish it from a merely possible assumption.

steps: Rewrite the claim in neutral wording.
Identify the conclusion and the reasons offered for it.
Ask “what must also be true for these reasons to support this conclusion?”
Generate possible missing premises.
Select the premise most necessary to the inference, not merely an interesting background belief.
Test it with a counterexample: if the premise were false, would the argument weaken?
Classify the premise as supported, unsupported, contested or unnecessary.
Rewrite the argument with the premise made explicit.
practice_protocol.frequency_per_week: Analyse three to five short arguments per session. Include arguments that are sound as well as weak ones to prevent reflexive fault-finding.
practice_protocol.environment: Use short, non-sensitive claims with enough context to interpret

assessment.method: Given five arguments, identify a relevant necessary or highly material assumption in at least four, explain why it matters, and distinguish it from a merely possible assumption.
assessment.record: Annotated arguments, identified premises, counterexample tests, support classification and delayed cold analysis.

maintenance.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance.protocol: Use a fresh argument after several days. Score relevance and explanatory justification, not the number of assumptions generated.

maintenance_policy.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance_policy.protocol: Use a fresh argument after several days. Score relevance and explanatory justification, not the number of assumptions generated.
maintenance_policy.scheduler_note: A review interval is earned by performance evidence, not assigned from category alone.

safety_notes: Avoid personal attacks. Critique reasoning and evidence rather than inferring hidden intent or character.

records.name: Separate fact, inference, and opinion
records.definition: Label statements by evidential status and explain ambiguous cases.

target_performance.statement: Classify statements by what is directly observed or verifiable, what is inferred from evidence, and what expresses evaluation or preference.
target_performance.metric: At least 12 of 15 statements are classified with defensible reasons; compound statements are split; and uncertain or predictive claims are not forced into a simplistic category.
target_performance.conditions: Use a short article, report or everyday scenario with traceable source material. Recognise that a sentence can contain more than one claim and may need splitting.

success_criteria.statement: Classify statements by what is directly observed or verifiable, what is inferred from evidence, and what expresses evaluation or preference.
success_criteria.threshold_text: At least 12 of 15 statements are classified with defensible reasons; compound statements are split; and uncertain or predictive claims are not forced into a simplistic category.

steps: Break compound sentences into individual claims.
Mark direct observations or independently checkable records as factual claims, while noting that the source may still be wrong.
Mark conclusions that go beyond the observation as inferences and write the evidence supporting them.
Mark value judgements or preferences as opinions and identify the value standard behind them.
Flag predictions, causal claims and uncertain statements separately when the three-way label is insufficient.
Find one statement whose label changes when more evidence is supplied.
Rewrite ambiguous statements to show what is known and what is inferred.
practice_protocol.frequency_per_week: Classify 10–15 statements in a session. Discuss borderline cases rather than forcing certainty.
practice_protocol.environment: Use a short article, report or everyday scenario with traceable source material

assessment.method: At least 12 of 15 statements are classified with defensible reasons; compound statements are split; and uncertain or predictive claims are not forced into a simplistic category.
assessment.record: Passage annotations, source links, reasons for classifications, uncertainty flags and delayed classification result.

maintenance.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance.protocol: Reclassify a new passage after a delay. Include at least two ambiguous cases and justify uncertainty.

maintenance_policy.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance_policy.protocol: Reclassify a new passage after a delay. Include at least two ambiguous cases and justify uncertainty.
maintenance_policy.scheduler_note: A review interval is earned by performance evidence, not assigned from category alone.

safety_notes: Do not expose private information in examples. Preserve context and avoid presenting allegations as facts.

records.name: Create a retrieval prompt
records.definition: Turn a learning objective into a question requiring genuine recall or reasoning.

target_performance.statement: Convert a learning objective into questions that require retrieval and reasoning rather than recognition or copying.
target_performance.metric: A reviewer can identify the target objective for every prompt; the set covers recall, explanation, application, discrimination and transfer; and the answer guide distinguishes correct reasoning from keyword matching.
target_performance.conditions: Start from a clear objective and the material it refers to. Identify what the learner should recall, explain, perform, compare or transfer.

success_criteria.statement: Convert a learning objective into questions that require retrieval and reasoning rather than recognition or copying.
success_criteria.threshold_text: A reviewer can identify the target objective for every prompt; the set covers recall, explanation, application, discrimination and transfer; and the answer guide distinguishes correct reasoning from keyword matching.

steps: Rewrite the objective as an observable action.
Draft one free-recall prompt with no answer cues.
Draft one explanation prompt asking why or how.
Draft one application prompt using a changed example.
Draft one discrimination prompt asking when a rule does not apply.
Draft one transfer prompt that changes context or constraints.
Check that each prompt tests the objective rather than trivia.
Write a concise answer key or rubric, including acceptable variants and common misconceptions.
Pilot the prompts without notes and revise questions that are ambiguous or too easy to guess.
practice_protocol.frequency_per_week: Create a five-prompt set per learning objective. Keep prompts short enough to answer, but do not make them so leading that they reveal the answer.
practice_protocol.environment: Start from a clear objective and the material it refers to

assessment.method: A reviewer can identify the target objective for every prompt; the set covers recall, explanation, application, discrimination and transfer; and the answer guide distinguishes correct reasoning from keyword matching.
assessment.record: Objective, five prompts, answer guide/rubric, pilot responses, revision notes and delayed performance.

maintenance.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance.protocol: Use the prompts after a delay and record which prompt exposes a genuine gap. Revise prompts that repeatedly produce false positives.

maintenance_policy.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance_policy.protocol: Use the prompts after a delay and record which prompt exposes a genuine gap. Revise prompts that repeatedly produce false positives.
maintenance_policy.scheduler_note: A review interval is earned by performance evidence, not assigned from category alone.

safety_notes: Use accurate answer keys and disclose uncertainty where content is contested.

records.name: Error log analysis
records.definition: Record an error, diagnose its cause, and select a corrective practice.

target_performance.statement: Turn repeated mistakes into a specific diagnosis and a targeted corrective practice rather than merely recording that an answer was wrong.
target_performance.metric: For at least four recent errors, the learner identifies the earliest faulty step, gives a defensible cause, chooses a targeted correction, and demonstrates improvement on a new item of the same type.
target_performance.conditions: Use a recent exercise, coding task or project with enough work shown to trace the error. Avoid recording passwords or sensitive personal data.

success_criteria.statement: Turn repeated mistakes into a specific diagnosis and a targeted corrective practice rather than merely recording that an answer was wrong.
success_criteria.threshold_text: For at least four recent errors, the learner identifies the earliest faulty step, gives a defensible cause, chooses a targeted correction, and demonstrates improvement on a new item of the same type.

steps: Capture the original task and the exact point of failure.
Preserve the attempted reasoning or steps before correcting it.
Classify the error: knowledge gap, misinterpretation, procedure, calculation, attention, tool/environment, or strategy.
Ask what evidence distinguishes the chosen category from alternatives.
Identify the earliest incorrect step, not only the final wrong answer.
Write a corrective rule or test that would catch this error next time.
Create one near-transfer practice item targeting the same failure mechanism.
Reattempt without looking at the correction and compare.
practice_protocol.frequency_per_week: Log only meaningful errors; review 3–5 at a time. A large log without diagnosis or action is not useful.
practice_protocol.environment: Use a recent exercise, coding task or project with enough work shown to trace the error

assessment.method: For at least four recent errors, the learner identifies the earliest faulty step, gives a defensible cause, chooses a targeted correction, and demonstrates improvement on a new item of the same type.
assessment.record: Original attempt, error location, classification and rationale, corrective test, new-item result and recurrence record.

maintenance.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance.protocol: Review the log after one week. Check whether the same error recurs and whether the corrective rule catches it. Preserve recurrence history.

maintenance_policy.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance_policy.protocol: Review the log after one week. Check whether the same error recurs and whether the corrective rule catches it. Preserve recurrence history.
maintenance_policy.scheduler_note: A review interval is earned by performance evidence, not assigned from category alone.

safety_notes: Keep logs private where appropriate; do not store confidential code, account details or personal data.

records.name: Estimate before calculating
records.definition: Generate a plausible range before exact calculation.

target_performance.statement: Produce a reasonable magnitude or range before exact calculation, then use the estimate to detect implausible results.
target_performance.metric: For at least four of five tasks, the estimate is within a pre-agreed reasonable range, the unit is correct, and the learner can use the estimate to catch an intentionally planted implausible answer.
target_performance.conditions: Use calculations where units and approximate magnitudes are understood. State assumptions; do not estimate in place of exact work where safety or precision requirements demand exact measurement.

success_criteria.statement: Produce a reasonable magnitude or range before exact calculation, then use the estimate to detect implausible results.
success_criteria.threshold_text: For at least four of five tasks, the estimate is within a pre-agreed reasonable range, the unit is correct, and the learner can use the estimate to catch an intentionally planted implausible answer.

steps: Read the problem and identify the quantity being asked for.
Write the unit and expected scale (ones, tens, hundreds, etc.).
Round inputs to convenient values while preserving the order of magnitude.
Calculate a rough result mentally or with simple arithmetic.
Record an interval if uncertainty is meaningful.
Perform the exact calculation separately.
Compare exact result with the estimate and explain any large discrepancy.
Check units and whether the result makes sense in the original context.
practice_protocol.frequency_per_week: Use five varied problems per session: whole-number arithmetic, decimals/percentages, ratios, measurement and real-life quantities. Keep estimates distinct from exact answers.
practice_protocol.environment: Use calculations where units and approximate magnitudes are understood

assessment.method: For at least four of five tasks, the estimate is within a pre-agreed reasonable range, the unit is correct, and the learner can use the estimate to catch an intentionally planted implausible answer.
assessment.record: Written estimate made before exact work, units, assumptions, exact result, discrepancy explanation and delayed unseen result.

maintenance.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance.protocol: Repeat with unseen problems after a delay. Include a problem where rounding in the wrong direction creates a misleading estimate.

maintenance_policy.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance_policy.protocol: Repeat with unseen problems after a delay. Include a problem where rounding in the wrong direction creates a misleading estimate.
maintenance_policy.scheduler_note: A review interval is earned by performance evidence, not assigned from category alone.

safety_notes: For financial, construction, medical or electrical decisions, estimation is only a sanity check and must not replace required exact calculation or qualified verification.

records.name: Chunk a procedure
records.definition: Convert a multi-step task into meaningful stages and cues.

target_performance.statement: Group a multi-step procedure into meaningful units that preserve order, decision points and error checks, then reconstruct it without losing critical steps.
target_performance.metric: A learner can reconstruct the complete procedure from chunk labels, preserve all critical decision points and safety checks, and explain when a chunk cannot be skipped.
target_performance.conditions: Choose a procedure with a clear start and finish, such as a software workflow, study routine or safe household task. Do not compress safety-critical instructions in ways that remove warnings.

success_criteria.statement: Group a multi-step procedure into meaningful units that preserve order, decision points and error checks, then reconstruct it without losing critical steps.
success_criteria.threshold_text: A learner can reconstruct the complete procedure from chunk labels, preserve all critical decision points and safety checks, and explain when a chunk cannot be skipped.

steps: Perform or inspect the full procedure once and list every action in order.
Mark decision points, dependencies and steps where errors are costly.
Group adjacent steps that serve one purpose into named chunks.
Give each chunk a short label describing its outcome, not just its first action.
Write the trigger for moving to the next chunk and any verification check.
Test the chunking by explaining the full sequence from the labels alone.
Reopen the detailed steps and check that no exception, warning or dependency was lost.
Practise the chunks in order, then vary one non-critical condition and explain what changes.
practice_protocol.frequency_per_week: Chunk one procedure at a time. Aim for a small number of meaningful groups; do not force a fixed chunk count across different tasks.
practice_protocol.environment: Choose a procedure with a clear start and finish, such as a software workflow, study routine or safe household task

assessment.method: A learner can reconstruct the complete procedure from chunk labels, preserve all critical decision points and safety checks, and explain when a chunk cannot be skipped.
assessment.record: Original ordered steps, chunk map, decision/checkpoint list, cold reconstruction, source comparison and transfer attempt.

maintenance.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance.protocol: Reconstruct the procedure after a delay from chunk labels, then compare with the authoritative procedure. Any omitted critical step requires relearning.

maintenance_policy.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance_policy.protocol: Reconstruct the procedure after a delay from chunk labels, then compare with the authoritative procedure. Any omitted critical step requires relearning.
maintenance_policy.scheduler_note: A review interval is earned by performance evidence, not assigned from category alone.

safety_notes: For medical, electrical, workshop or emergency procedures, never simplify away warnings or replace certified instruction. Use the authoritative procedure as source of truth.

steps: Identify the zero mark; do not assume the metal hook edge is the zero reference without checking its movement design.

steps: Identify whether bleeding is severe, spurting, persistent, associated with a serious object or accompanied by faintness or major injury.

Dispose of contaminated materials safely.

success_criteria.statement: Align a map with the surrounding landscape using visible landmarks and distinguish map direction from the learner’s facing direction.

steps: Identify the map’s north indicator and scale/legend.

steps: Identify the direction-of-travel arrow, magnetic needle and bearing scale on the specific compass.

Rotate the housing to the instructed bearing using the compass model’s markings.
Turn your body until the needle aligns with the orienting arrow as taught for that compass.
Select a visible safe landmark along the bearing rather than walking while staring at the compass.
Walk to the landmark, stop and re-check.
Note magnetic interference and local declination only when the map/route requires it and the learner has been taught how.

records.name: Doomsday Algorithm (weekday mental calculation)
records.definition: Calculate the weekday for a Gregorian calendar date using a taught algorithm, explain leap-year handling and verify edge cases.

target_performance.statement: Given a Gregorian calendar date, calculate its weekday using a named anchor method and show intermediate values so arithmetic or century-rule errors can be located.
target_performance.metric: For 20 unseen dates spanning ordinary years, leap years, January/February and century exceptions, achieve at least 18 correct and show a valid calculation path for every answer. A correct guess without traceable reasoning is not sufficient.
target_performance.conditions: Use the Gregorian calendar only. Learn one published Doomsday method from a reliable mathematics reference; do not mix month codes from different methods. Begin with dates in a familiar non-leap year.

success_criteria.statement: Given a Gregorian calendar date, calculate its weekday using a named anchor method and show intermediate values so arithmetic or century-rule errors can be located.
success_criteria.threshold_text: For 20 unseen dates spanning ordinary years, leap years, January/February and century exceptions, achieve at least 18 correct and show a valid calculation path for every answer. A correct guess without traceable reasoning is not sufficient.

steps: Memorise the seven-day cycle and the century anchor for the selected method.
Learn the year-anchor calculation in separate parts: century contribution, last two digits, floor division by four, and final modulo-seven reduction.
Learn month anchor dates for ordinary years.
Apply the leap-year adjustment only for January and February in leap years.
Work each date on paper, writing every intermediate value and reducing modulo seven at the end.
Check answers against an independent calendar.
Practise century boundaries and leap-year exceptions only after ordinary cases are reliable.
When an answer is wrong, identify whether the error came from the anchor, year arithmetic, month code, leap-year adjustment or weekday mapping.
practice_protocol.frequency_per_week: 10–15 dates per short session, split by difficulty. Do not practise speed until accuracy is stable; use mixed dates rather than repeating one month.
practice_protocol.environment: Use the Gregorian calendar only

assessment.method: For 20 unseen dates spanning ordinary years, leap years, January/February and century exceptions, achieve at least 18 correct and show a valid calculation path for every answer. A correct guess without traceable reasoning is not sufficient.
assessment.record: Written intermediate calculations, date set, answer key source, error classification, cold delayed test.

maintenance.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance.protocol: Repeat 10 unseen dates after 3–7 days without reviewing month codes immediately beforehand. Relearn the specific component responsible for any error.

maintenance_policy.trigger: Delayed cold retrieval after a meaningful delay
maintenance_policy.protocol: Repeat 10 unseen dates after 3–7 days without reviewing month codes immediately beforehand. Relearn the specific component responsible for any error.
maintenance_policy.scheduler_note: A review interval is earned by performance evidence, not assigned from category alone.

safety_notes: This is a low-risk mental arithmetic skill. Do not treat calendar calculation as evidence about historical date accuracy; calendar reforms and local adoption dates can matter.

records.definition: Encode an ordered set of information using familiar locations and retrieve it in sequence with low error.

target_performance.statement: Use a familiar, stable route to encode and retrieve an ordered set of information, while verifying recall rather than relying on vividness alone.
target_performance.metric: Recall at least 9 of 10 items in correct order immediately and after a delay, with meanings accurate rather than merely recalling the associated image. Record intrusions and order swaps.

success_criteria.statement: Use a familiar, stable route to encode and retrieve an ordered set of information, while verifying recall rather than relying on vividness alone.

steps: Walk the route mentally in a fixed direction and name each location in order.
Assign one information item to each location.
Create a distinctive, concrete image that links the item to the location; exaggeration may aid distinctiveness but should not obscure the item.
Keep one item per locus during initial learning.
Mentally walk the route and retrieve each item without looking at the list.
Check exact wording or meaning against the source.
Repair weak loci with a more distinctive association.
Practise forward retrieval first, then selected reverse or random retrieval only when ordered recall is stable.

records.name: French Drop (basic coin-vanish sleight)
records.definition: Perform a simple coin-vanish illusion with controlled hand positioning, natural timing and an honest performance context.

target_performance.statement: Perform a simple coin-transfer illusion in which the audience’s attention is directed to an apparent receiving hand while the coin remains concealed in the other hand.
target_performance.metric: In five trials for a consenting observer, the apparent transfer should be plausible in at least four, while the coin remains secure and no unnatural hand posture is visible. The learner must also be able to reveal and recover the coin safely.
target_performance.conditions: Use one ordinary coin of a size that is comfortable to handle. Practise seated over a clear table or soft surface. Learn the movement from a reputable beginner magic source and focus on naturalness rather than speed.

success_criteria.statement: Perform a simple coin-transfer illusion in which the audience’s attention is directed to an apparent receiving hand while the coin remains concealed in the other hand.
success_criteria.threshold_text: In five trials for a consenting observer, the apparent transfer should be plausible in at least four, while the coin remains secure and no unnatural hand posture is visible. The learner must also be able to reveal and recover the coin safely.

steps: Hold the coin visibly between the thumb and fingers of the dominant hand in a relaxed, repeatable position.
Bring the receiving hand toward the coin as if to take it, keeping the action smooth and unhurried.
Practise the concealed retention of the coin in the original hand slowly without performing for an audience.
Rehearse the receiving hand closing naturally as though it contains the coin; avoid exaggerated squeezing.
Coordinate gaze and head orientation with the apparent transfer only after the hand action is mechanically consistent.
Practise both hands separately in a mirror or video.
Perform the sequence for a trusted observer and ask where they believed the coin went.
Adjust only one variable at a time: finger tension, timing, gaze or hand path.
practice_protocol.frequency_per_week: Use 3–5 minute sets with breaks. Stop if repetitive finger tension causes discomfort.
practice_protocol.environment: Use one ordinary coin of a size that is comfortable to handle

assessment.method: In five trials for a consenting observer, the apparent transfer should be plausible in at least four, while the coin remains secure and no unnatural hand posture is visible. The learner must also be able to reveal and recover the coin safely.
assessment.record: Practice video or observer feedback, coin-control success, hand tension notes and delayed performance.

Record which transition causes instability and isolate that transition.
